items.title: Sherrie Maricle interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 18, 2001 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: Well thinking of the two biggest singer breakthroughs, Harry Connick in the recent decade and Diana Krall

ctx.x: I’ve heard some complaints, mostly from what I have to describe as middle-aged white players, that the record companies these days, if they’re going to back up somebody it’s most likely going to be somebody pretty young and black. Is there any truth to that statement do you think?

Well thinking of the two biggest singer breakthroughs, Harry Connick in the recent decade and Diana Krall, and this new woman that’s being pushed pretty hard, Jane Monheit, they’re all white. No I can think of some, Jackie Terrason and I can think of

some young white artists. But yeah, I don’t know, you look at records here at this festival there’s hundreds of records downstairs with phenomenal players. I don’t understand how like media and marketing works but you could take any musician and I’m sure if you dump enough advertising into them they’re going to have a little flicker of fame. Like as great as Diana Krall is, who I love her, I happen to be a really big fan of hers, I love the way she plays, I think she’s great, but I know some other players who do…
